I will keep my land mainly in the usual wheat-maize rotation, because that fits Quzhou County best, matches my labor ability, and gives me the most stable food and cash outcome over a full year. I will grow winter wheat on the land first, then follow it with summer maize after wheat harvest. I am 44, farming in a place where water matters and weather can turn hard, so I will not chase complicated crops this year. I will use improved seed for wheat because it is steady and familiar, and hybrid seed for maize because the yield is better and the stand is usually stronger. I will keep fertilizer at a moderate level instead of pushing too hard, because too much input raises cost and risk. I will use rotary tillage because it is practical for me and easier to manage on time. For irrigation, I will give wheat more attention since it needs moisture at key stages, while maize will get fewer waterings unless the season turns dry. I will also keep pesticide sprays limited and only plan for the common disease and insect pressure I expect in a normal year. My goal is steady production, manageable labor, and lower risk across the whole season.
